title: Letter 24 — Communion with Christ
attribution_note: Letter 24 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: Thou wouldest know what a Christian is, and requirest of me a brief explanation? I set before thee out of Holy Scripture what communion and union Christians have with Christ, the Son of God. Read this, and consider it diligently. From this thou mayest know also for thyself what a Christian is, and of what sort he must be who would be a true Christian.
The communion of Christians with Christ is marked in Holy Scripture after this manner:
Christ is the *“Light,”* and Christians are they that are enlightened (see [John 1:9]).
Christ is the *“Life,”* and Christians are they that are made alive (see [John 11:25]).
Christ is the *“Shepherd,”* and Christians are the *“sheep”* (see [John 10:2, 14; 1 Peter 2:25]).
Christ is the *“way,”* and Christians are travellers [John 14:6].
Christ is the *“foundation,”* and Christians are the building (see [1 Corinthians 3:9, 11; Ephesians 2:20–22]).
Christ is He that dwelleth within, and Christians are the Church (see [Ephesians 3:17; 2 Corinthians 6:16; 13:5]).
Christ is the *“Firstborn,”* and Christians are brethren (see [Colossians 1:18; Romans 8:29]).
Christ is the *“vine,”* and Christians are the *“branches”* (see [John 15:5]).
Christ is the *“Bridegroom,”* and Christians are the *“bride”* (see [Matthew 25:1–13; 2 Corinthians 11:2]).
Christ is the *“Head,”* and Christians are the *“body,”* that is, a spiritual body (see [Ephesians 1:22–23; 1 Corinthians 12:27]).
Christ is the *“Heir,”* and Christians are joint-heirs (see [Hebrews 1:2; Romans 8:17]).
Thou seest the communion of Christians with Christ. This we see in the Scripture, and especially in the epistles of the holy apostle Paul.
From this thou mayest know:

1) What a true Christian is, and not a false one — that is, he who hath a living and heartfelt faith in Christ, the Son of God, and liveth holily and godly in Christ Jesus. Holy is the Head, holy is the Vine, holy is the Bridegroom; holy also must His members be, holy also the branches, holy also the bride. Else, *“what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?”* [2 Corinthians 6:14]

2) From this thou seest how high and exalted is the nobility and dignity of true Christians. To have communion and friendship with an earthly king is most glorious; how much more incomparably glorious is it to have communion with the Heavenly King, the King of kings and Lord of lords!
3) Thou seest that from this holy society they are shut out who sin against conscience, though they think that they are within the Church.

4) Having known what a true Christian is, labour to be such; for knowledge alone without the deed is nothing. For what profit is it to know the light and to be in darkness; to know the good and not to seek the good; to see the table and not to taste of the table? And if thou wilt and labourest to be a Christian, then flee from every sin.
Be saved.
